findings.title: Deletion can still precede every durable forward-cleanup authority
findings.observation: cleanupForwardRestoreProject awaits cleanupOwnedProject, which can delete the complete frozen set and return PASS, before persistForwardRestoreCleanupEvidence writes any replayable authority. The recovery branch only applies when that file already exists. After a process death in between, re-entry sees QUIESCING with a nonempty frozen set, no forward evidence and an empty live project; cleanupOwnedProject treats the empty/nonempty set difference as failure.
findings.trigger: Create a READY restore lifecycle, let cleanupOwnedProject complete all deletions and return PASS, then terminate before line 2226 writes forward-restore-cleanup.json. Resume through cleanupForwardRestoreProject or executeRollbackWithCleanup.
findings.impact: Although all exact attempt-owned resources are already gone, recovery converts the successful cleanup to FAIL, persists CLEANUP_FAILED, and the real rollback path ends ROLLBACK_FAILED. The forward cleanup is therefore not replayable across the full mutation boundary and requires manual intervention after a benign process failure.

evidence.description: A review-only exact-head regression simulated deletion completion before the forward evidence write. Re-entry returned FAIL instead of PASS; the temporary test was removed and the worktree returned clean.

A fresh-context independent reviewer exercised the actual executeRollbackWithCleanup path after the same crash point. It observed zero live resources and no second deletion, but terminal ROLLBACK_FAILED and lifecycle CLEANUP_FAILED.
The irreversible cleanup call completes at line 2215, while the first forward authority write begins at line 2226; the recovery branch at lines 2175-2212 requires the evidence file to exist.
The committed crash test manually writes forward-restore-cleanup.json before replay, so it covers evidence-written/lifecycle-not-written but not deletion-complete/evidence-not-written.
The approved design requires replay/live reconciliation of completed cleanup authority and places persistence, idempotency and recovery under the same lifecycle contract.

findings.remediation: Make the deletion-to-authority sequence recoverable at every process boundary. Persist a durable operation/journal before or during deletion, or safely reconcile QUIESCING plus missing forward evidence plus an empty live project against the frozen exact authority and reconstruct the same PASS result. Do not turn an already empty, exactly frozen project into cleanup failure solely because the evidence write did not occur.
findings.verification: Add a regression that crashes after the final delete and quiescence proof but before forward-restore-cleanup.json is written, then enters executeRollbackWithCleanup and requires ROLLED_BACK, a resolvable PASS authority, CLEANED restore lifecycle and no second delete.

required_actions.action: Close the deletion-before-evidence crash window and prove actual rollback replay reaches ROLLED_BACK without another delete.

risks.description: A process failure after successful restore deletion but before its evidence write can turn a safe empty state into ROLLBACK_FAILED.
risks.mitigation: Block merge until PRR-001 provides durable progress or exact empty-state reconciliation across this boundary.

risks.description: No production deployment, DNS, public endpoint, real secret or production database was exercised in Review.
risks.mitigation: Keep production execution behind the separate release authorization and acceptance workflow.
